subsystems.name: Neural sensing
subsystems.role: turns brain activity into a measurable signal.

subsystems.name: Stimulus and task protocol
parts: flicker patterns for steady-state visual evoked potentials

subsystems.name: Signal conditioning
parts: artefact rejection for eye blinks, muscle and movement

subsystems.name: Feature extraction and matching
subsystems.role: converts cleaned signal into a compact identity signature and compares it.

subsystems.name: Template store and liveness checks
subsystems.role: holds enrolled signatures and blocks fakes.

subsystems.name: Consent and data governance
subsystems.role: handles neural data, which cannot be reissued like a password.

buildSteps.title: Choose the sensing modality
buildSteps.detail: Scalp EEG is cheap and non-invasive but noisy; implanted electrodes give far better signal-to-noise at surgical risk and cost.

buildSteps.title: Design the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the user rests quietly, looks at flickering targets or responds to rare stimuli, and how long a check must take to be acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Enrol the person
buildSteps.detail: Record several sessions on different days, at different times, so the template captures normal day-to-day variation rather than one lucky recording.

buildSteps.title: Preprocess the recordings
buildSteps.detail: Filter to the relevant bands, detect and discard contaminated epochs, and keep enough clean data per session.

buildSteps.title: Extract identity features
buildSteps.detail: Compute band power, evoked-response shape and cross-electrode coupling, then reduce these to a compact signature.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the matcher
buildSteps.detail: Set the decision threshold against target false-accept and false-reject rates, testing how the signature drifts across weeks and after caffeine, sleep loss or medication.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with anti-spoofing
buildSteps.detail: Require a live, cooperative subject, detect replayed recordings, and combine the neural check with a conventional factor so a misread cannot stand alone.

buildSteps.title: Re-enrol and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Refresh templates periodically and watch for slow drift, since a neural signature is not as fixed as a fingerprint.

prerequisites.why: research-grade EEG works in a lab, but consumer headsets give unstable signals once the user moves or sweats.
muscle, eye and motion noise dominate real-world recordings and can imitate or mask a signature.
a recorded brain signal or a synthetic one can be replayed into the matcher unless liveness is proven.
invasive arrays record better but degrade over months to years and need surgery.
neural data can leak health and cognitive information, and unlike passwords it cannot be reset.

pathway.milestone: laboratory studies showing that resting-state and evoked EEG patterns can distinguish individuals in small groups
pathway.unlocks: evidence that brain signals carry identity information at all.

pathway.milestone: longitudinal trials measuring accuracy across months and outside the lab
pathway.unlocks: realistic error rates and an understanding of how much re-enrolment is needed.

pathway.milestone: combination with established biometrics and hardware liveness detection
pathway.unlocks: use as a second factor in high-security settings such as research facilities and controlled rooms.

pathway.milestone: continuous authentication on wearable or implanted neural interfaces
pathway.unlocks: identity confirmed moment to moment during brain-controlled device use — the closest thing to the tile's claim, and still nothing like 'absolute'.
